overview.problem: Assimilate the Thalon and Swordfish engineering-efficiency frameworks into Eamos across five bundles: parallel-workflow tooling (native worktree symlinks + preinstall guard + an adapted contract-window skill), agent-handoff leanness, CI/repo safety hardening + ops safety nets, a single metered LLM gateway choke point, and structural ratchet tests as the sole cross-code wiring tracker while graphify is decommissioned entirely. Every enforcement gate lands in three moves (Measure -> Conform -> Enforce) so no blocking gate ever meets a non-conforming repo.
overview.approach: Seven dependency-ordered waves; every enforcement gate lands in three moves (Measure -> Conform -> Enforce) so no blocking gate ever meets a non-conforming repo. W1 lands independent foundation artifacts (backend + web boundary ratchets green, repo grep-guard, hardened handoff-lint, the with_gateway_guard choke point, worktree scripts, contract-window skill, renovate) -- every tracked-file scanner CRLF-safe and every .ps1 pure ASCII for PowerShell 5.1. W2 is the CONFORM wave: M-012 reshapes CURRENT.md to the lean 5-heading zero-append form that passes strict handoff-lint, and M-017 drives the backend ruff/black residual and the web next-build to zero -- both BEFORE any gate for them is flipped. W3 ENFORCES the pre-commit hook (installer + exit-code-gated body running the strict lint), depends_on M-012 so the hook never blocks a commit on a non-conforming CURRENT.md. W4 wires the three package.json manifests (prepare -> install-hooks; preinstall worktree guard). W5 is the single CI-enforcement milestone owning ci.yml -- SHA-pin + least-priv + zizmor -- and is ENFORCE-ONLY: it depends_on M-017 (ruff/black + next-build conformed) and M-012 (handoff conformed) and only then flips each gate to blocking behind one stable aggregate 'ci' required check; it makes no Conform edits. W6 decommissions graphify across ALL surfaces (both skill dirs, both agent-hook systems, every governance copy, the memory note, the active RISKS.md line, and the ignore/scan refs), M-014/M-015/M-016 each depends_on M-013 so removal happens strictly after the boundary ratchets are enforced in CI. W7 (M-018) then scrubs every LIVE graphify reference across the 28 docs/** living specs/plans and runs the repo-wide `git grep -in graphify` completeness sweep -- proving only the dated PROGRESS.md/CHANGELOG.md build-log history and the agent_handoff/archive/** snapshots remain (docs/ is NOT blanket-tombstoned) -- with M-018 depends_on M-013 + M-014/M-015/M-016 so the final sweep runs after every sibling scrub. Each shared file gets exactly one owning milestone.

decisions.decision: Full-remove graphify; executable structural boundary ratchets become the sole cross-code wiring tracker.
decisions.reasoning: graphify is a documentary-tier tracker plus a 510 MB artifact and an API-costed semantic pass -> executable structural tests are a higher ratchet tier, zero cost, and go red on wiring drift -> the enforcement role transfers to tests; the user chose FULL REMOVE, accepting loss of semantic navigation -> delete every graphify artifact, hook, rule, and doc reference.

decisions.decision: Fixed ordering: boundary ratchets are green and enforced in CI BEFORE any graphify artifact or rule is removed.
decisions.reasoning: Removing the old tracker before the replacement is enforced opens a wiring-blind window where drift ships unnoticed -> gate all graphify-removal milestones on the CI-enforcement milestone -> the decommission wave depends on the CI wave.

decisions.decision: Every enforcement gate ships in three moves: Measure (report-only) -> Conform (drive the repo to zero) -> Enforce (flip to blocking in CI + pre-commit).
decisions.reasoning: Flipping a blocking gate onto a non-conforming repo red-walls every PR -> measure the existing violation count first, size the Conform effort from it, reach zero, then enforce -> ruff/black and next-build gates especially need the Conform pass before the flip.

decisions.decision: The web boundary ratchet is a node guard script (scripts/eamos-web-boundary.mjs), not a new vitest harness.
decisions.reasoning: app/web carries no vitest config and standing one up is scope creep -> the existing test:protein-architecture shows app/web already runs node-guard checks -> implement the web boundary as a .mjs guard reusing the established eamos-*.mjs pattern.

decisions.decision: One metered gateway choke point wraps budget-assert -> trace span -> call -> record usage -> end span; the request path uses per-user + global daily caps, the offline CLI path uses an operator/global token budget.
decisions.reasoning: Caps live at the route layer today, not around the call, and the embed/materialize CLIs bypass them -> wrap every AIGatewayEngine call in with_gateway_guard so budget + span + usage are uniform -> keep two budget modes because forcing a per-user cap onto operator CLIs is wrong; the span ends even on error before the exception rethrows.

decisions.decision: CURRENT.md root cause is append surfaces + local-only lint, not loose thresholds; the fix is CI-tier strict lint plus a 5-heading overwrite-whole-file form with zero append surfaces.
decisions.reasoning: A linter already existed yet CURRENT.md drifted to 483 lines because it ran only from a local untracked hook, non-strict, only when CURRENT.md was staged -> raise the ratchet to executable tier by running strict handoff-lint in CI, and remove the append ledgers (overwrite-whole-file, history in git) so the file cannot grow.

decisions.decision: Each shared integration file gets exactly one owning milestone (one-file-one-milestone), matching the one-web-writer-per-wave rule.
decisions.reasoning: Many bundles touch the same shared files (ci.yml, settings.json, the three package.json, governance markdown) -> two milestones editing one file clobber each other -> group edits by owning file so ci.yml, settings.json, and the governance docs each land in a single coordinated milestone.

decisions.decision: The settings.json worktree.symlinkDirectories block rides the gated config-decommission milestone because it shares the file with the graphify PreToolUse hooks.
decisions.reasoning: worktree.symlinkDirectories and the graphify nudge hooks both live in .claude/settings.json, and graphify-hook removal is gated after CI enforcement -> under one-file-one-milestone both settings.json edits ride the gated milestone -> the worktree scripts and package guards land earlier so parallel work is unblocked; only the auto-symlink convenience waits.

decisions.decision: The grep-guard scans git-tracked files only, assembles secret/conflict tokens from fragments, and its exit code gates both the pre-commit hook and a required CI check.
decisions.reasoning: CI sees only committed files via git grep, and Swordfish leaked a guarded name because the guard's exit code never gated the commit -> Eamos scans tracked files, builds forbidden secret-shape tokens from fragments so the guard passes its own scan, and gates on exit code -> Eamos guards secret shapes + merge-conflict markers (not brand-hiding, since Eamos is the private product repo).

decisions.decision: Never npm install inside a worktree; a preinstall guard aborts it and installs run in the main checkout, visible to lanes via native symlinks with a junction fallback.
decisions.reasoning: npm v7+ deletes the linked node_modules and forks the lane's dependency tree -> a preinstall guard detects a worktree via .git being a FILE and exits 1 -> installs happen once in the main checkout and worktree.symlinkDirectories (junction fallback without Developer Mode) makes them visible to every lane.

decisions.decision: CI required-check stability comes from one aggregate 'ci' job: needs:[all] + if: always() + an explicit per-need success assertion.
decisions.reasoning: Branch protection references a check by name and a shard/re-org renames it, and a skipped required check can silently pass -> an aggregate job that asserts every need succeeded gives one stable required name that cannot pass on a skip.

decisions.decision: SHA-pin every GitHub Action to a digest, add least-privilege permissions blocks, add a zizmor workflow static-analysis job, and keep pins fresh with renovate.
decisions.reasoning: Mutable @v4/@v5 tag refs are a supply-chain risk and the workflows carry no permissions block -> pin actions to digests, set 'permissions: contents: read', and lint workflows with zizmor -> renovate helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests maintains the pins so hardening does not rot.

decisions.decision: Keep the Eamos three-lockfile structure; do not convert to a turbo/nx/pnpm unified monorepo. Assimilate tooling and leanness only.
decisions.reasoning: A Python backend plus two JS surfaces with separate lockfiles means monorepo unification is large churn for marginal gain -> port the parallel-workflow tooling, gateway choke, ratchets, and leanness without touching the repo's structural shape.

decisions.decision: The contract-window skill is adapted to Eamos: freeze Pydantic schemas plus both TS mirrors, additive-only, mirror-diff ratchet via the existing test_frontend_contract.py canary; drop Thalon's drizzle/zod/tenant_id/events specifics.
decisions.reasoning: Thalon's SOP assumes drizzle/zod/tenant_id/events that Eamos lacks -> adapt the freeze targets to app/backend/app/schemas/*.py + app/web/lib/backend.ts + app/frontend/src/lib/backend.ts, keep additive-only + the mirror-diff ratchet + one lead owner per sprint, and freeze the contract at merge.

decisions.decision: Every graphify surface is enumerated and removed, classified by half-life -- NOT blanket-excepted. SCRUBBED as live references: both skill dirs (.claude/skills/graphify + the duplicate .agents/skills/graphify), both agent-hook configs (.claude/settings.json PreToolUse + .codex/hooks.json), the nested .claude/CLAUDE.md '# graphify' trigger block, the graphify sections in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/CODEX.md plus the graphify-update rule, the dedicated memory note memory/graphify-generated-output-hygiene.md and its MEMORY.md wikilink, the stale graphify-command line in agent_handoff/RISKS.md, the graphify AST-update fire-drill in docs/parallel-agents/ratchet-philosophy.md, the dead graphify-out refs in .gitignore/.worktreeinclude/scripts/eamos-encoding-scan.mjs, AND -- newly in scope -- every LIVE graphify reference in the 28 docs/** living specs/plans (procedural `python -m graphify update .` steps, `graphify update is Codex's lane`, `graphify community 537; do not touch it`, `graphify first`/`graphify-confirmed`/`graphify edge` method notes), which a repo-wide `git grep -in graphify` audit surfaced and which are living planning artifacts, NOT dated build-logs, so they are scrubbed by the new M-018. The TOMBSTONE exception is narrowed to genuinely-dated append-only build-log history ONLY: PROGRESS.md and any same-class CHANGELOG.md session entries, plus the agent_handoff/archive/** dated handoff snapshots -- rewriting a dated log falsifies the audit record. docs/ is NO LONGER blanket-tombstoned. Completeness is PROVEN by M-018's repo-wide sweep: `git grep -in graphify -- ':!PROGRESS.md' ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!agent_handoff/archive/'` must return zero lines (agent_handoff/CURRENT.md is left graphify-free by M-012's lean reshape).
decisions.reasoning: DL-001 mandated removing EVERY graphify artifact/hook/rule/doc reference, and an earlier pass blanket-classified ALL of docs/ as a historical tombstone -> a live repo-wide `git grep -in graphify` audit disproves that: 28 docs/** files carry LIVE graphify references (procedural `graphify update` steps, the `graphify update is Codex's lane` coordination rule, the `graphify community 537; do not touch it` instruction, `graphify first`/`graphify-confirmed` method notes) that are living planning artifacts, not dated append-only session logs -> classify strictly by half-life: only genuinely-dated build-log history (PROGRESS.md/CHANGELOG.md session entries + agent_handoff/archive/** dated snapshots) is tombstoned, because rewriting a dated log falsifies the audit record; docs/** living specs/plans are IN-SCOPE for scrub -> add M-018 to scrub every live docs/** reference AND run a repo-wide `git grep -in graphify` completeness sweep that returns only the dated tombstones, so DL-001's 'delete every doc reference' mandate is machine-provable, not asserted.

decisions.decision: Windows / PowerShell-5.1 quirks are baked as acceptance criteria into each script the plan creates: .ps1 files are pure ASCII and run under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with no pwsh dependency (invoked as `& scripts/x.ps1`); worktree teardown uses `cmd /c "rmdir /s /q"`, never PS Remove-Item -Recurse; every tracked-file line scanner (backend/web boundary ratchets, grep-guard, handoff-lint) is CRLF-safe (line-start match, strip trailing CR); the pre-commit hook gates on each guard's exit code with no exit-swallowing chaining; eamos-worktree-setup verifies and re-sets repo-local git identity; and the preinstall guard aborts only when .git is a regular FILE, failing open when .git is absent or a directory.
decisions.reasoning: Thalon burned real leaks/corruption on these exact Windows traps (a semicolon-chained guard committed and pushed a leaked token because the exit code was ignored; PS Remove-Item -Recurse followed a junction and wiped MAIN node_modules; a BOM-less .ps1 parsed as ANSI and broke; CRLF made whole-line `=======` conflict-marker matches miss and shipped committed markers) -> encode each quirk as a binding acceptance criterion on the artifact it touches so the ratchet is actually correct on this box -> the guard's fail-open-unless-.git-is-a-FILE rule additionally guarantees it cannot block a CI / Vercel / Render full-clone install.

decisions.decision: Thalon parallel-workflow governance ports land in AGENTS.md/COORDINATION.md: the lead drives review/rebase/PR/CI-watch/merge/post-merge-wiring end-to-end (founder does only founder-only actions); launching any lane or subagent needs fresh per-session founder approval and approval covers exactly the named runs (each reviewer agent and each fix-round resume is a separate launch); Mode-B (the 'vscode method' — founder-opened terminals at lead-prepped worktrees via eamos-worktree-setup.ps1) is the preferred parallel mode; a dead lane's worktree is inspected/salvaged before any redo; and cheap provably-non-breaking (net-positive) speedups are taken in-run without trading correctness, safety, or approval protocols.
decisions.reasoning: Eamos already has propose-lanes + LEAD-sole-merger but not the per-launch-approval, Mode-B-prep, dead-lane-salvage, or net-positive-speedup disciplines Thalon paid for (a 2-lane approval ballooned to 6 agent runs; a dead lane's worktree was nearly redone from scratch though it held committed work + global installs) -> port them as named conventions tied to the eamos-worktree-setup.ps1 tooling this plan adds -> subagent runs are the dominant spend so approval is per-launch, the worktree script is what makes Mode-B prep mechanical, and inspect-before-redo prevents duplicated work.

decisions.decision: No AI attribution in Eamos GitHub commits or PRs; follow Thalon's convention (attribution: {commit: '', pr: ''} in .claude/settings.json plus the governance-doc rule). Founder directive 2026-07-09, OVERRIDING the earlier keep-the-Co-Authored-By-trailer guidance.
decisions.reasoning: Founder: 'i dont want anything co-authored by ai to appear in the github, so follow thalon on that' -> the Claude Code harness auto-adds a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` commit trailer and a robot `Generated with Claude Code` PR footer, and the only clean suppression is the settings.json `attribution` block Thalon/Swordfish already use -> port it IN-SCOPE (the settings.json edit rides the settings.json-owning milestone M-014 per one-file-one-milestone, the positive rule goes in the governance docs M-015), record that it supersedes the prior Co-Authored-By mandate, and scope it going-forward only (a retroactive history scrub is a separate, destructive, out-of-scope decision).

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: User chose FULL REMOVE; the semantic-navigation role is intentionally dropped in exchange for zero-cost, red-on-drift structural enforcement.

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Huge churn across a Python backend + two JS surfaces with separate lockfiles for marginal gain.
Windows-only quirk (npm v7 clobbers linked node_modules); native worktree.symlinkDirectories via Developer Mode is preferred, junction only as fallback.
Eamos has no drizzle/zod/tenant_id/events; the SOP must be adapted to Pydantic schemas + two TS mirrors.

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Deferred; only the single metered gateway choke point is pulled from the LLM bundle this cycle.

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: app/web has no vitest config; a node guard reusing the eamos-*.mjs pattern is lighter and matches the existing test:protein-architecture idiom.

rejected_alternatives.alternative: Just loosen the handoff-lint thresholds so the 483-line CURRENT.md passes.
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Treats the symptom; the root cause is append surfaces + local-only lint, fixed by CI-tier strict lint + a zero-append-surface schema.

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Not applicable to Eamos: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and CODEX.md are independent files (verified distinct inodes, link count 1), not hardlinked. They are kept as synced copies edited individually; there is no hardlink to sever, so the Swordfish recreate-and-verify ratchet is unneeded here.

constraints: Windows: never cd; use git -C / npm --prefix / a subshell only.
Explicit pathspecs on every git add/rm; never git add -A.

Agent-agnostic ownership; shared-doc edits go through the Log Edit-Lock; schema-first contracts stay in lockstep (Pydantic app/backend/app/schemas/*.py + app/web/lib/backend.ts + app/frontend/src/lib/backend.ts).
No flag/provider/env flips without Steven; never run vercel from app/web; deploy from the repo root only; vault access is read-only; never echo secrets.
Reuse existing Eamos assets, no duplicates: extend the nine eamos-*.mjs guards, scripts/hooks/pre-commit, and scripts/eamos-handoff-lint.mjs; do not duplicate them.
agent/* lanes go through PR + CI + human-approved merge; never --admin-bypass the gate.
Surgical changes: every changed line traces to a named ported Thalon/Swordfish pattern; match existing style.
Fixed ordering (user): boundary ratchets are green + enforced in CI before any graphify artifact or rule is removed.
Native non-admin symlinks require Windows Developer Mode (SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege); a junction fallback covers the no-Dev-Mode case.
Out of scope: turbo/nx/pnpm monorepo; VPS self-host / Swordfish Bucket-6 migration; the full eval-as-CI-gate harness; flag/provider/env flips; any deploy.
No Docker and no admin elevation on the IT-monitored Windows work box (founder policy): local tooling is user-scope only; heavy or Linux-only work runs in CI / cloud, never a local container.

Windows PowerShell 5.1 is the only PowerShell (no pwsh): repo .ps1 files are pure ASCII and invoked directly (& scripts/x.ps1); multi-line git messages go through a file (git commit -F <file>); never rewrite repo files via PS string surgery (UTF-8/CRLF corruption); worktree dirs are deleted with cmd /c "rmdir /s /q", never PS Remove-Item -Recurse.

risks.risk: Backend ruff/black Conform effort is unknown; the linters are not even installed and the gate has never run.
risks.mitigation: Measure first (ruff check app/backend --statistics; black --check app/backend), size the Conform pass from the count, and keep the autoformat as its own isolated commit.

risks.risk: Flipping a blocking gate onto a non-conforming repo red-walls every PR.
risks.mitigation: Three-move rollout; the Enforce flip is conditional on the Conform pass reaching zero.

risks.risk: Removing graphify before the boundary ratchets are enforced opens a wiring-blind window.
risks.mitigation: Fixed ordering: every graphify-removal milestone depends on the CI-enforcement milestone.

risks.risk: worktree.symlinkDirectories yields copies or junctions rather than real symlinks without Windows Developer Mode.
risks.mitigation: eamos-worktree-setup.ps1 provides a junction fallback and a doctor-style verify; document Developer Mode (SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege) enablement.

risks.risk: Consolidating the scattered gateway calls could break the offline embed/materialize CLI path, which uses a different budget model.
risks.mitigation: with_gateway_guard supports two budget modes; the LLM call-site inventory is pinned by test_boundary so a missed site fails the build.

risks.risk: Enabling strict handoff-lint on a non-conforming CURRENT.md would red-wall commits/PRs. The --strict gate has TWO Enforce surfaces (the pre-commit hook AND the CI job), each of which must be sequenced after the single Conform.
risks.mitigation: M-012 (wave W-002) reshapes CURRENT.md to the lean zero-append form that passes --strict -- the CONFORM. Both Enforce surfaces are sequenced strictly after it and each declares an explicit milestone dependency on M-012: (1) the pre-commit hook eamos-handoff-lint --strict in M-010 (wave W-003, depends_on M-012) and (2) the CI strict handoff-lint job in M-013 (wave W-005, depends_on M-012). Neither Enforce surface can land in the same or an earlier wave than the M-012 Conform.

risks.risk: A repo-wide black/ruff autoformat pass can collide with concurrent feature edits (notably the gateway consolidation).
risks.mitigation: The ruff/black Conform runs as the dedicated M-017 pass (wave W-002) -- a final residual format-only sweep, after each code milestone (M-001/M-002/M-006) has already left its owned files ruff/black-clean -- so the sweep is a no-op on owned files and collides with no concurrent feature edit; M-013 (wave W-005) only flips the gate to blocking, making no format edits itself.

risks.risk: The preinstall worktree guard (guard-worktree-install.mjs, .git-is-a-FILE detection) could abort a legitimate npm install during a CI / Vercel / Render production build and break the deploy.
risks.mitigation: The guard aborts ONLY when .git is a regular FILE (a real worktree); it fails open (exit 0) when .git is absent (git archive / shallow tarball) or is a directory (a normal full clone). CI, Vercel, and Render all install from full clones (.git is a directory), so the guard never fires there; M-007 pins this with an explicit fail-open test.

risks.risk: Editing repo files or line-matching them through Windows PowerShell 5.1 corrupts UTF-8 / mis-handles CRLF (BOM-less files read as ANSI; a whole-line '=======' match misses a CRLF-terminated marker; a non-ASCII .ps1 parses wrong).
risks.mitigation: Edit repo files via the harness Write/Edit tools, never PS string surgery; every tracked-file scanner strips a trailing CR and matches at line start; .ps1 artifacts are pure ASCII. Baked into M-002/M-003/M-004/M-005/M-007 acceptance.

risks.risk: The no-AI-attribution port suppresses attribution GOING FORWARD only; Eamos's existing commit history already contains Co-Authored-By trailers.
risks.mitigation: Scope is new commits/PRs only (the settings.json attribution block + the governance rule). Retroactively scrubbing existing trailers requires a git history rewrite + force-push to main, which is DESTRUCTIVE -- it breaks the parallel-agent branch protection and any collaborator/worktree clones -- so it is a SEPARATE founder decision explicitly NOT in this plan unless the founder asks.

invisible_knowledge.system: Ratchet-strength ladder (Thalon AGENTS.md, mirrored in Eamos docs/parallel-agents/ratchet-philosophy.md): executable (test/CI/constraint) > structural (seam/type/schema) > configuration (tracked settings) > documentary (rule/runbook) > memory/chat (lost). Leave every ratchet as high as it goes and route each lesson to one home, pruning the stale copy. This is WHY graphify (documentary) yields to structural boundary tests (executable), and WHY handoff-lint moves from a local hook to CI. The handoff drifted to 483 lines DESPITE a linter because the linter ran only in a local untracked hook, non-strict, only when CURRENT.md was staged, never in CI or a worktree lane; Thalon's CURRENT.md stays ~45 lines because it has zero append surfaces (overwrite-whole-file; history in git). The gateway is consolidated into one with_gateway_guard choke point so budget assertion, trace span, and usage recording are uniform across the request path (per-user + global caps) and the offline CLI path (operator/global budget). Shared integration files each get one owning milestone; ci.yml is the single enforcement surface with an aggregate stable 'ci' required check.
invariants: Every LLM call routes through the single with_gateway_guard choke point; the LLM call-site inventory is pinned by test_boundary.py.
os.environ / os.getenv is read only in app/backend/app/core/config.py, with an enumerated exception list (core/sentry.py, cli/eamos_crispr_score_preflight.py).
Route modules stay thin: no direct import of repository or database internals.
No merge-conflict markers exist in any git-tracked file.
Every enforcement gate ships Measure -> Conform -> Enforce; a blocking gate never lands on a non-conforming repo.
The CI required check is one stable aggregate 'ci' job that cannot pass on a skipped or failed need.
grep-guard and the boundary ratchets scan git-tracked files only.
npm install never runs inside a worktree; installs happen in the main checkout and reach lanes via symlink/junction.
Schema-first contracts stay in lockstep: Pydantic app/backend/app/schemas/*.py + app/web/lib/backend.ts + app/frontend/src/lib/backend.ts; additive-only within a contract window.
The boundary ratchets are green and enforced in CI before any graphify artifact, hook, rule, or doc reference is removed.
The preinstall worktree guard aborts only when .git is a regular file; it fails open on a directory .git (normal clone) or an absent .git, so it can never block a CI/Vercel/Render production install.
Every tracked-file scanner (boundary ratchets, grep-guard, handoff-lint) is CRLF-safe: it strips a trailing CR and matches at line start, never by whole-line equality.

The graphify decommission is complete only when git grep -i graphify is empty across both skill dirs, both agent-hook configs (.claude/settings.json + .codex/hooks.json), every governance copy (CLAUDE/AGENTS/CODEX/.claude/CLAUDE), the memory note + its MEMORY.md wikilink, the active guardrail doc agent_handoff/RISKS.md, docs/parallel-agents/ratchet-philosophy.md, the ignore/scan refs, agent_handoff/CURRENT.md (graphify-free after M-012's lean reshape), AND every one of the 28 docs/** living specs/plans (scrubbed by M-018). The tombstone exception is narrowed to dated build-log history ONLY -- PROGRESS.md / CHANGELOG.md session logs and agent_handoff/archive/** dated handoff snapshots -- because rewriting a dated log falsifies the audit record; docs/ is NOT blanket-tombstoned. Completeness is PROVEN by M-018's repo-wide sweep: `git grep -in graphify -- ':!PROGRESS.md' ':!CHANGELOG.md' ':!agent_handoff/archive/'` returns zero lines.

No AI attribution in commits/PRs going forward: .claude/settings.json sets attribution.commit and attribution.pr to empty and CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/CODEX.md state the no-attribution rule; retroactively scrubbing existing-history trailers is explicitly out of scope (a destructive history rewrite = separate founder decision).

The 3-move ordering is encoded as explicit milestone dependencies (depends_on) the QR can verify: the Conform milestones M-017 (ruff/black residual + next-build, W-002) and M-012 (handoff, W-002) precede every Enforce surface -- M-010 depends_on M-012 (pre-commit strict lint, W-003) and M-013 depends_on {M-017, M-012} (CI gates, W-005) -- and the graphify-removal milestones M-014/M-015/M-016 each depends_on M-013 (removal only after CI enforcement). No blocking gate flips in the same or an earlier wave than the milestone that drove the repo to zero for it.
tradeoffs: Semantic navigation of the >5000-node repo is intentionally dropped (full graphify removal) in exchange for zero-cost, red-on-drift structural enforcement.

The settings.json worktree convenience block lands late (gated with graphify-hook removal) to honor one-file-one-milestone; parallel-work capability arrives earlier via the worktree scripts and package guards.
Keeping three lockfiles (no monorepo) preserves the repo shape at the cost of forgoing unified workspace tooling.
The web boundary ratchet is a node guard rather than a test-runner suite, keeping web test infra light but placing the web ratchet outside a formal runner.

milestones.name: Pre-commit hook wiring (installer + hook body)
requirements: A tracked installer sets git core.hooksPath to scripts/hooks idempotently and degrades to a no-op when node is absent.
The pre-commit hook runs eamos-vercel-project-guard --require-root-link + eamos-grep-guard + eamos-handoff-lint --strict (when handoff files are staged), and each non-zero exit gates the commit.

The hook gates on each guard's exit code with explicit checks (set -e / if [ $? -ne 0 ]); it never chains guard + commit with a construct that ignores a non-zero exit, so a failing guard always aborts the commit (the semicolon-chaining trap that leaked a token on Thalon).

3-move discipline (DL-003) for the pre-commit ENFORCE surface: the hook's `eamos-handoff-lint --strict` step is an ENFORCE move that lands in wave W-003 strictly AFTER the M-012 CONFORM (wave W-002) reshapes CURRENT.md to the lean zero-append form that passes --strict. M-010 declares depends_on M-012 so the strict pre-commit lint can never activate before its Conform. (The same --strict lint is enforced again in CI by M-013 / wave W-005, likewise gated on the M-012 Conform.)

milestones.name: CI hardening + 3-move gate enforcement
requirements: Every action is SHA-pinned to a digest and every job carries a least-privilege 'permissions: contents: read' block; a zizmor workflow static-analysis job is added.

ENFORCE ONLY -- M-013 makes NO Conform edits. Every gate's Conform pass is completed in an EARLIER wave: ruff/black + web next-build by M-017 (wave W-002), strict handoff-lint by M-012 (wave W-002), and both boundary ratchets land green in wave W-001. M-013 (wave W-005) verifies the tree is at zero and only THEN flips ruff+black, next-build, grep-guard, strict handoff-lint, and both boundary ratchets to blocking. M-013 declares depends_on M-017 and M-012 so no gate flips blocking in the same or an earlier wave than the milestone that drove the repo to zero for it.

An aggregate 'ci' job needs:[all] + if: always() + an explicit per-need success assertion is the single stable required check; enforcing the boundary ratchets here satisfies the graphify-removal precondition (M-014/M-015/M-016 each depends_on M-013).
